correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge5\) the four neighbors are distinct. The five-bit local rule corresponds bijectively to indexed closed walks of length \(n\) on a sixteen-state de Bruijn graph. Exhausting the sixteen transition rows gives two directed five-cycles, one five-state strongly connected component with shared-vertex three- and five-cycles, and a dead state. Therefore \(\det(I-zA)=(1-z^5)^2(1-z^3-z^5)\). The trace-log identity yields the exact coefficient formula; deleting the formal \(3z^3\) term makes the generating function for \(n\ge5\) correct. The unique order-seven obstruction follows from the numerical semigroup generated by three and five. Irreducibility and \(\gcd(3,5)=1\) prove \(E_n/\rho^n\to1\). The standard-library checker independently reconstructs the transitions, enumerates every binary profile for \(5\le n\le17\), and verifies exact traces through order 120. Finite computation supports but does not replace the all-order proof.

originality.rationale: The primary arXiv:2301.11849 studies complexity of the identical nonmonotone best-response rule on general graphs, rather than enumerating its equilibria on four-neighbor squared cycles. Related arXiv:2301.11580 and 2207.04238 concern hardness and degree-two ordinary cycles, whereas arXiv:2406.01710 counts typical random-graph cellular-automata fixed points; accessible earlier special-family claims likewise do not entail the all-order rational generating function. Actual semantic and literature searches found no stronger covering result. An unindexed equivalent cellular-automata enumeration remains a plausible residual risk; this is a qualified comparison rather than a guarantee of bibliographic uniqueness.

value.rationale: It is a complete exact equilibrium count on a natural infinite family of four-regular social-interaction graphs for the nonmonotone response pattern whose general existence problem is hard. The enumeration proves a sharp exceptional network order with no pure equilibrium, eventual existence for every larger order, and a nontrivial exponential multiplicity rate. The explicit rational generating function provides reusable enumeration and structural insights well beyond routine application of a generic algorithm.
